title: KCS U4(b) measured: the first-order WIDTH NUMBER — the level-1 upper/lower sieve gap at reachable z, exact integers, 66 rows. Definitions: L1 = x - sum_{p<=z} floor(x/p) (level-1 lower), U2 = L1 + sum_{p<q<=z} floor(x/(pq)) (level-1 upper), W = U2 - L1 (exactly the pairwise mass), main term xV(z), exact count Phi (the 0180 object). Measured (kcs4b_width_number.py, tmp/kcs4b_out.txt, x in {2e5, 1e6..1e10}, pi(z) = 4..20, z <= 71, 7s): (i) the EXACT sandwich L1 <= Phi <= U2 on all 66 rows (0 violations) — the discrete level-1 upper/lower sieve property, named as the next Lean unit (level1_sandwich); (ii) Phi triple-checked exact (full-Mobius-sum = Legendre recursion = brute force at 2e5, 11/11) — the measured twin of discovery 0180; (iii) the width number W/(xV) grows in z: 2.1041 (z=7) -> 10.1249 (z=71) (the main term is a shrinking share of the level-1 band; W is the pairwise mass so W/(xV) ~ (sum_{p<q} 1/pq)/V(z)); (iv) the POSITION rho = (Phi - L1)/W of the exact count inside the band is x-stable to ~1e-6 and decreases in z: rho = 0.84158 (z=7) -> 0.67288 (z=71); rho0 = Phi/U2: 0.75000 -> 0.23191 — the exact count sits consistently ABOVE the band's midpoint at reachable z: the first number for the N3 'parity = the opacity' reading (the level-1 estimates carry no position information; the exact count's position inside the gap is what the orbit measures); (v) remainder Phi - xV <= 1194.6 absolute at the largest z vs the worst case 2^20 - 1 = 1048575 (877x margin, the grind not reached, twin of the U1a remainder table)
claim: No RH claim: pure finite sieve combinatorics over exact integers (no floats in any comparison; floats only print reported ratios). The sandwich L1 <= Phi <= U2 is an exact discrete fact at every measured (x, z) — the finite, integer, level-1 form of the classical upper/lower sieve property — and is stated as the next formal unit (a Lean theorem in the SieveOrbit family: even-order IE partial sums are upper bounds, odd-order are lower bounds, for the squarefree divisor sums). The width number and the position rho are measured, not asymptotic claims: the width table is 2.1041/2.8292/3.5731/4.2344/4.9013/6.0350/7.0265/7.9132/8.7275/9.4539/10.1249 for z = 7/11/13/17/19/29/37/43/53/61/71 and rho = 0.84158/0.80781/0.78184/0.76317/0.74740/0.72532/0.70952/0.69739/0.68755/0.67961/0.67288 at x = 1e10 (x-stable: the same columns at x = 1e6 differ by < 2e-5). The KCS N3 row is updated to: (a) proved (0180), (b) MEASURED (this entry), (c) the parity/anchor correspondence still pending (structural statement, not a barrier theorem).

structure noted in the output: W = U2 - L1 is EXACTLY the pairwise mass sum_{p<q} floor(x/(pq)) (the single-prime terms cancel between L1 and U2); L1 is negative for every z >= 5 in the sweep (sum_{p<=z} 1/p > 1), so the band's content is on the upper side and rho measures the exact count's position against a negative floor (honest caveat recorded in the table)
